mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is at or below 0.25%, the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to accommodative monetary policy reducing the cost of capital and increasing equity valuations.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS <= 0.25%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the average 20-day return in low-rate periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 7.5%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which often precedes a recession and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors flee risk.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 7.5%, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.5% annually and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains below 1.0%, the market perceives a 'dovish' monetary policy stance that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL annual inflation > 2.5% AND FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the average 20-day return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer demand (RSAFS > 400,000 and HOUST > 900), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy expands and corporate earnings grow.
failure_condition: When RSAFS > 400000 AND HOUST > 900, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the average 60-day return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 135,000 thousand persons signals a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 135000, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the average 20-day return in high-employment periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.5 (2017=100) signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 98.5, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) is rising (annual change > 2.0%) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising (change > 0.1% in the last month), the market perceives a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL annual inflation rate > 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.1%
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL annual inflation > 2.0% AND FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.1%, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the average 20-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production (INDPRO > 99.0), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy expands and corporate earnings grow.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 99.0, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the average 60-day return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
